## ORPHAN-HIGH-597 — the capacity gate could only reclaim images, and the space was never in images — RESOLVED (this PR)

**Discovered:** 2026-08-09, tracing why a disk freed the previous day was full again.

`deploy-capacity-maintenance` blocked with **1.24 GB free against a 37.5 GB hard floor**, and `safe_image_gc` had nothing to take: all 37 images backed running containers, so `docker system df` honestly reported **0 B reclaimable**. An image-only response reports "nothing to reclaim" beside a disk that is 98% full — a true statement and a useless one.

The space was in `TMPDIR`, and one pattern owned half the disk:

| pattern                  | directories |        size |
| ------------------------ | ----------: | ----------: |
| `nx-native-file-cache-*` |   **1,421** | **29.3 GB** |
| everything else in /tmp  |      ~8,500 |      ~34 GB |

Nx's native module resolves its cache through `std::env::temp_dir()` — verified in the shipped binary, which references `TMPDIR` and `temp_dir` and carries **no** dedicated cache-directory variable (the only `NX_*CACHE*` strings belong to the remote cache). It creates a fresh directory per workspace-process and nothing removes them: the age histogram shows 100-400 new directories a day since 2026-08-04. A manual sweep reclaimed 12.9 GB on 2026-08-08 and the disk was full again within a day, which is what makes it a gate concern rather than an operator chore.

**Fix:** `safe_tmp_gc`, a **separate** function beside `safe_image_gc`, invoked from the same "capacity is short" trigger. Separate on purpose: `safe_image_gc`'s banner promises "volumes/containers/networks/build-cache untouched", and widening it to sweep a filesystem would make that sentence false.

Its policy is default-deny and every clause is load-bearing: an explicit allowlist of patterns that are **regenerable by construction**, an age floor so an in-flight build never loses its cache, a per-candidate open-handle check, and `-maxdepth 1` under an absolute root so a pattern can never match deeper than the temp directory. It touches no checkout, worktree, ARIA state or session scratchpad.

**Proof:** 6 gate tests running the real function against a decoy TMPDIR — most of them assert what it must NOT delete, because a sweeper that reclaims space by removing someone's checkout is a worse outage than the full disk. Both breaks red: removing the invocation, and widening the allowlist to `aqua-*` (the checkout survives only because the allowlist is narrow).

**Manual reclaim performed alongside, with evidence per class:** stale Nx caches (open-handle-checked), clones proven clean _and_ whose HEAD is reachable from a remote branch, and worktrees of already-merged PRs. **4.1 GB → 35 GB free.** Four trees holding uncommitted work were left untouched, including one whose HEAD exists on no remote branch.

**NOT fixed, stated plainly:** this only reclaims. `TMPDIR` is what actually decides where Nx writes, so bounding the writer — pointing CI at a dedicated, size-capped temp filesystem — remains the stronger fix and is not done here. And 35 GB is still below the 37.5 GB floor: the gate will keep failing until the disk grows or a generation of images ages out.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED for reclaim; bounding the writer is open.

## ORPHAN-CRITICAL-596 — ten of twelve agent requests were permanently unreachable, and the prompt-hash check could never pass — RESOLVED (this PR)

**Discovered:** 2026-08-09, after the runtime and evidence fixes let agents run for the first time in five nights.

Two independent defects, both permanent rather than transient.

**1. The prompt-hash binding was unsatisfiable by construction.** `create_agent_invocation_request` attaches the Twin slice to the request row (`repository_map`), renders the prompt FROM that row, and hashes the result. The claim response then enumerates its envelope fields explicitly — and **omits `repository_map`** (and `cycle_id`). The executor rebuilds an envelope from that response and re-renders, so its prompt loses the entire `## Repository map` section and the hash cannot match. Every request whose `evidence_refs` resolve against the Twin map failed `prompt_hash_binding_mismatch` on **every** claim, forever. Two serialisers carried the same omission — `claim_request` and `planner_dispatch_hook` — which is why fixing one would have looked like a fix and changed nothing.

**2. Claims leaked, and the leak had no exit.** Measured on production state: **10 of 12** requests had `claimed` as their latest event with no release. `derive_request_state` reaches `PENDING` from `CLAIMED` only through an explicit released/requeued event; once the 30-minute lease expires the state derives `STALE`, which `next_pending_request` skips and `claim_request` refuses. Both exits closed — the request is dead, and nine baseline-carrying requests sat behind the dead ones.

Three holes fed it:

- The submit-failure path was the **one** exit in `ci_executor.main` that did not release, so a rejected result held its claim forever.
- `_release_claim` never read the subprocess return code: a release that FAILED was indistinguishable from one that happened, and the executor walked away reporting only its original error.
- `reap_stale_claims` **existed** and was reachable only from the operator CLI — no cycle phase, no workflow. Its sibling `dispatch_lease_reap` runs every cycle but reaps `dispatch/claims.jsonl`, a different ledger. The agent-invocation ledger had no automatic reaper at all, which is how it looked covered.

**Fix:** the claim response carries `repository_map` and `cycle_id` in both serialisers; the submit path releases under `submit_rejected`; `_release_claim` reads its return code and announces a failed release as an `::error::` saying the request stays CLAIMED; and `reap_stale_claims` becomes a cycle phase beside its sibling. Requeue stays bounded by `DEFAULT_MAX_REQUEUES`, so a poisonous request escalates to `HUMAN_REQUIRED` rather than cycling.

**Two corrections to my own earlier reading, recorded because both were wrong in the same direction:** the executor does NOT resume in-flight work (the workflow picks the id via `agent next-pending`, which only returns PENDING/REQUEUED — the "resume in-flight work" line is an advisory string from the handoff snapshot); and the empty `actual=` in the mismatch message was a log artefact, not the defect — the real empty was the rendered repository-map section.

**Proof:** 6 tests, AST node-shape rather than source text (Plan 026R §H.1). The strongest asserts that **every `return 1` branch after the claim is taken contains a `_release_claim`** — the invariant the submit path broke. All three fixes reverted individually, all three went red. Full kernel suite green (3,464 tests).

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-621 — three quality dimensions had zero adapters, and schema-drift was a farm-only property — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. Discovered 2026-08-10 during the end-to-end ARIA read (FAZ 7 of the "Sinir Sistemi" program; the fleet-coverage gap the mission charter's D1-D6 dimension model made visible).

The adapter fleet covered D1-security and D4-testability; **D2-performance, D5-documentation and D6-correctness(parity) had no watcher at all**, and `typeorm-entity-schema-adapter` scanned only `apps/farm-service` while six sibling services carry the identical per-tenant schema discipline (ADR-011) unwatched.

**Fix — three deterministic v1 adapters (manifest + TS, fleet pattern, SHADOW):**

- `bundle-budget-adapter` (D2): flags an MFE with no declared bundle budget (no `chunkSizeWarningLimit`, no `bundle-budget.json`) and heavyweight libraries imported statically (welded into the initial chunk). Real-repo first run: **9 findings** — no MFE declares any budget.
- `doc-staleness-adapter` (D5): resolves every backtick-quoted repo path in `docs/**/*.md` against the working tree; a reference to a deleted path is a finding (globs/placeholders/`:line` refs handled). Real-repo first run: **1,146 findings across 1,271 docs** — the documentation debt is now measured instead of suspected.
- `fe-dto-parity-adapter` (D6): AST-collects backend `*Dto` classes and hand-written frontend `*Dto` types (generated files excluded — they are the fix, not suspects); same name + different field sets = drift finding naming missing/extra fields. Real-repo first run: **2 findings, both in `web/modules/admin-panel/src/services/types/` — exactly the hand-written-types disease the SSOT audit documented.**

**typeorm widening:** multi-service sweep over the 7 schema-per-tenant services (explicit `root` keeps the single-service call shape for fixtures). Widening exposed a latent FP class: the migration-registry check assumed farm's class-import registry, while sibling services legitimately register a GLOB in `data-source.ts` — every such service would have flooded `migration_registry_missing_entry`. The check now detects the registration style first; measured differential: farm-only findings **214 → 95** (the removed 119 were the glob-style false class), multi-service total 404 → 194.

**Proof:** 4 self-asserting adapter test scripts green (fleet pattern); registry compiles 9 tools; real-repo smoke runs recorded above; fixture `real-repo-baseline` cases added per adapter.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-620 — the daily report had two writers and zero published readers: the lane committed an empty anchor stub while the real report and every dashboard ledger accumulated unread — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. Discovered 2026-08-10 during the end-to-end ARIA read (FAZ 6 of the "Sinir Sistemi" program).

**Two writers, one filename.** The daily-report lane generated its anchor from the EPHEMERAL checkout's empty `aria-tools` (no state restore in the generate job), committed the stub, and opened a PR whose body was three empty lines and a filename. Meanwhile reflection wrote the real operator report to the durable store's `reports/daily/<date>.md` every cycle — same filename class, never published, zero readers.

**Ledgers written every cycle, read by nothing:** `compute_plan_016_metrics` had no scheduled caller; `observability`'s `dashboards.jsonl` (SLO state, alerts) had zero readers; mission events reached no operator surface; quarantine state was CLI-only; FAZ 1's replay recall landed in the sealed cycle row and stopped there.

**Fix (one report):** the generate job restores aria/state first (contract: `first_governed_mutation_step=_RESTORE_STEP`, `github_git` declared, store write root allowed — mirroring the producer/eval lanes); `emit_anchor_to_path` composes the anchor frontmatter WITH the reflection report body from the store when present (`render_anchor_markdown(body_markdown=…)`) so the published artifact IS the report; the PR body carries the report's leading sections instead of three empty lines. Reflection gains five sections — Plan-016 counters, SLO/alerts, missions, quarantined tools, judge-replay recall — each the FIRST reader of its ledger, each silent (not scaffolded) on an empty store. `plan_016_metrics.write_dashboard` stays as the operator CLI verb; the data SSoT (`compute_plan_016_metrics`) is shared, not copied.

**Proof:** 10 tests: content-pin (published artifact contains the report body, not the anchor stub), stub fallback, idempotency preserved, each section's first-read, silence-on-empty, and the lane contract pin (restore-first + github_git). Workflow parity gate green after the contract/YAML/fixture moved together.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-618 — the environment contract existed only as prose: a mandatory merge gate with zero producers, and a claim path that discovered the broken host after spending the claim — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. Discovered 2026-08-10 during the end-to-end ARIA read (FAZ 5 of the "Sinir Sistemi" program).

Four organs, one theme — the environment's obligations were written down and never measured, so every environment fault was priced on the work (MISSION_SPEC M-2.5: two failures, two names):

**1. `verify_runner_attestation` was MANDATORY at merge and NOTHING produced a row.** The merge authority requires an attestation for every (pr_number, head_sha, readiness_claim_id) triple (`merge_authority.py:98`), the ledger is a first-class state surface — and a repo-wide search found zero writers. The gate could only ever raise `runner_attestation_required_for_merge`.

**2. The correct pre-claim shape lived only in a dead loop.** `claim_and_dispatch_one` (the operator `--consume` path with no CI caller) preflighted Claude auth BEFORE touching the queue; the CI path (`ci_executor.main`) claimed first and discovered the broken host after — a night with no auth or no sandbox burned a claim + requeue per request, escalating healthy requests toward HUMAN_REQUIRED.

**3. A blocked night and an idle night rendered identically.** The daily anchor carried counters but no cause; the operator could not tell "nothing to do" from "could not run".

**4. The nightly producer ran with no preflight at all — and the documented strict soft-warn had NEVER fired.** `verify_preflight` skipped `standard` entirely. Worse, found while wiring: the strict warn branch sat under `not verdict.valid`, and non-autonomous verdicts are always valid by construction (`valid = profile != "autonomous" or …`) — the branch was structurally unreachable since it shipped.

**Fix:** `probe_runner_attestation` + `probe_runner_attestations_for_claims` (PROBED, not self-asserted: sandbox via the runtime's own `sandbox_backend()` accessor, auth/API-key via the env the CLI actually authenticates with; config-asserted identity fields labeled as such in the row; a host that cannot attest is REFUSED — that refusal is the contract working). New `runner-attestation probe` CLI verb + `probe-runner-attestation` composite action wired into both lanes at start. `ci_executor` gains `_pre_claim_environment_gate` (claude auth / sandbox / node deps) that refuses BEFORE claiming and writes `claude_auth_unavailable` / `sandbox_unavailable` / `env_deps_missing` governance rows. `build_daily_anchor` derives an additive `blocked_reason` list from the same ledger (tier-2 automatic — no caller cooperation). `verify_preflight` measures the environment subset for every run profile; the orchestrator's verdict handling is extracted to `_apply_preflight_verdict`, keyed on reasons instead of the always-true flag, so the soft-warn is finally reachable — pinned by a direct test.

**Proof:** 15 tests: the probed row satisfies the previously unsatisfiable merge gate; re-probe idempotent per triple; sandboxless host refused; gate-before-claim position pinned; mock mode skips; standard preflight measures; warn-reachability pinned both directions; anchor carries the night's refusals and renders empty on a healthy night. Neighbour suites green (349), workflow contract + injection + sha-pin invariants green.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-617 — ARIA wrote what it learned every cycle and never read any of it back into a dispatch — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. Discovered 2026-08-10 during the end-to-end ARIA read that produced the "Sinir Sistemi" program (FAZ 4).

Three organs of the learning loop's READ side were dead, so every agent dispatch rediscovered the repository from zero:

**1. Conventions had a writer and no production reader.** `record_convention` has appended a row to `aria-tools/knowledge-graph/conventions.jsonl` on every converged cycle since V9.0-F. The only reader, `lookup_pattern` (`knowledge_graph.py:339`), was keyed by `pattern_id` and had **zero callers** — nothing anywhere resolved a pattern id, so no learned convention ever reached an agent.

**2. Beliefs fed pressure ranking, never the agent about to edit the believed-about files.** `latest_beliefs` was consumed by the pressure path only; the envelope minted for an agent touching `apps/farm-service/**` carried no trace of what ARIA had already verified about that exact area.

**3. `rank_pressure_sources` (`knowledge_graph.py:376`) had zero callers of any kind** — not even a test — while the calibration-recommendation section asked the operator to approve weight changes with no effectiveness data in view.

**Why mint-time matters (the binding constraint):** the prompt hash is sealed over the rendered text at mint, and the claim path re-renders from the fused envelope (`fuse_prompt_envelope`). Knowledge injected at claim or dispatch would either break the binding or bypass it. So both new sections — `## Established knowledge` (beliefs + conventions intersecting the request's evidence/scope paths) and `## Recent intent` (per evidence file, the last commits' subject + first WHY line + ADR/plan/finding refs — this repo's commit bodies are WHY-rich by convention, so intent reading starts from cited history) — are computed inside `create_agent_invocation_request`, stored as envelope data, added to `_FUSED_ENVELOPE_KEYS`, and sealed under the minted hash. Both render with the repository map's trust framing: projection, **not evidence**.

**Fix:** `conventions_for_paths` (first production read of the conventions ledger, same verified-chain discipline as `lookup_pattern`); `intent_context_for_files` in twin.py (deterministic, git-derived, never raises into the mint path); mint-time enrichment + renderer sections + fusion-set entries; `rank_pressure_sources` wired into the calibration-recommendation phase and rendered in its report section (first caller).

**Proof:** 12 tests. The binding pair is the deliberate break: dropping `established_knowledge` from the fused envelope fails hash reproduction (the fusion-set addition is load-bearing), and because the binding alone cannot detect a mint that silently stops attaching the sections, the rendered text itself is content-pinned. The claim-envelope AST guard (`test_claim_envelope_binding`) derives the renderer's key set mechanically, so the two new renderer keys could not have shipped without joining the fusion set. Neighbour suites green (212 tests), invariants green (803).

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-622 — the mission seeder validated itself against a shape its producer never emits, and the first live cycle failed on it — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. Discovered 2026-08-10 by the FIRST live auto-cycle over the neural-wiring pipeline (run 31437241716): phase `service_mission_seed` failed with `'list' object has no attribute 'get'` and the cycle sealed as failed.

**Root cause:** `impact_graph.cycle_service_examination` emits `per_service_pressures` as a **list** of `{service, layer, pressures}` groups in topological order. The FAZ 3 seeder read it as a dict keyed by project (`per_service.get(project)`), and — the deeper defect — its unit test **invented the dict shape** in its fixture, so the suite validated the consumer against data the producer never produces. The live cycle that found this is the FAZ 8 harness doing its job — the failure was recorded, phase-contained (`record_and_continue` kept sibling phases running), and the state store persisted the evidence.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-625 — runner-contract updates never reached the runtime: the sync re-registered birth statuses, the matrix read lifecycle advances as demotions, and refused silently — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. Discovered 2026-08-11 supervising the first post-#1173 live cycle (run 31466792131): tenant-scoping-adapter failed `budget_exceeded` AGAIN, two cycles after its timeout fix "merged".

**Root cause chain, each link verified:** `run_tool` reads the runner definition from the LIVE registry (aria/state `tools/registry.json`), not the repo manifest. The registry row still carried `timeout_ms: 180000` (and NO `node_max_old_space_mb` — the #1165 heap contract had never landed either; the OOMs stopped only because the runner's default happened to suffice). `_phase_tool_manifest_sync` re-registers every manifest each cycle — but passes the manifest's `status` verbatim, and the tool's live status had advanced SHADOW→CALIBRATE, so `register_tool` refused every re-registration as a demotion (`'CALIBRATE' -> 'SHADOW' must route through transition_tool()` — reproduced in isolation). The refusal was recorded in a phase result nobody surfaced: manifest said one thing, runtime did another, nothing said why.

**Fix:** the manifest's `status` is the BIRTH status; the live lifecycle owns it afterward. On re-registration the sync now carries the LIVE status, which routes through the matrix's same-status lane ("manifest hash drift → allow; parser/runner update") — built for exactly this. Quarantine is not weakened but strengthened: QUARANTINED re-registers as QUARANTINED (contract refreshes, status survives, audited unquarantine stays the only way back) — the old test asserted the refusal COUNT and is updated to assert the status property it actually cared about.

**Proof:** new test reproduces the live defect end-to-end (register SHADOW → transition CALIBRATE → manifest update → sync → timeout 420000 lands AND status stays CALIBRATE) + quarantine-survives test; 114 registry/sync/quarantine tests green.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-637 — the nightly executor consumed ONE request per run against a producer that mints many per cycle: the agent queue could only grow — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH. ## ORPHAN-CRITICAL-645 — the implementation state machine had no entry and plans died with their cycle: ARIA could implement perfectly and still record nothing — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: CRITICAL (Kapalı Döngü E2; audit F1+F9, both adversarially CONFIRMED). Every night's agent work landed on an abandoned plan.

**Fix (each transition written by its step's OWNER):** the envelope mint IS the CONVERGED→REQUESTED transition (idempotent, written after the append so a failed mint leaves the plan untouched); the result bridge brings REQUESTED→IN_FLIGHT with the REAL claim data the response carries before recording the outcome; the implementer poll accepts IMPLEMENTATION_RECORDED as the phase's success (MERGED belongs to the operator-gated merge chain); and a new `implementation_reconciler` folds RECORDED→MERGED from GitHub's own answer about the recorded PR — the operator merges, ARIA observes (never merges itself). Plan continuity: `resume_candidate_plan_id` — a new cycle ADOPTS the newest mid-convergence plan; drainer persistence is plan-keyed, not cycle-keyed. 6 new tests (full chain to RECORDED, merged-fold + idempotence, unmerged left alone, adoption) + 425 neighboring convergence/implementation tests green; TerminalState invariant deliberately extended with the WHY.

## ORPHAN-CRITICAL-644 — convergence was self-cancelling, in-cycle dispatch pointed at a tree with no code, and the coverage critic raised TypeError on every poll — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: CRITICAL (Kapalı Döngü E1). An independent end-to-end audit found the autonomous arc has nine full stops; these are the three earliest, and each alone ends the run.

**F2 — the independence gate was unsatisfiable by construction.** `convergence_drainer` claimed every role under ONE identity (`convergence:<pid>`), and `independence_check.verify_principal_disjointness` reads exactly that field from the claims ledger and calls a shared id an echo chamber. So every CONVERGED verdict was downgraded to `cross_review_self_agreement` by ARIA's own gate, and `autonomy_orchestrator` skips worker dispatch, implementation and auto-merge on any non-converged verdict. Convergence could never survive itself. Fixed: one dispatch per role, each claiming under `convergence:<pid>:<role>` — one process, but genuinely distinct actors with distinct prompts, evidence and outputs.

**F3 — in-cycle dispatch resolved its executor inside the STATE tree.** `_default_ci_executor_path` (and its worker twin) computed `base_dir.parent / tools/aria-poc/...`, which was correct while ledgers lived at `<repo>/aria-tools`. After the durable-store cutover `ARIA_TOOLS_DIR` is `<repo>/.aria-state-store/tools`, so the path resolved inside the state-branch worktree — ledgers, no code. Every in-cycle dispatch spawned a nonexistent file (exit 2), the plan state never moved, and the claim already taken was held for the whole lease window. No caller ever overrode the default. Fixed: both executor paths, `PYTHONPATH` and `cwd` resolve from the CODE tree (the package's own location), with the legacy arithmetic kept only as an installed-layout fallback.

**F6 — the coverage critic could not be dispatched at all.** The call omitted the required keyword-only `agent_id`, so it raised TypeError on EVERY poll iteration into a bare `except: pass`. The critic was minted, never claimed, and `_read_critic_adjudication` always polled to its deadline and fail-closed every waived node to "uncovered" — burning a convergence round each cycle, silently. Fixed: the required identity is passed (role-scoped, same reason as F2) and a failure now writes a governance row instead of vanishing.

4 new tests incl. a deliberate-break pinning the pre-fix identity shape against the REAL gate reader; 260 neighboring convergence/dispatch/independence tests green.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED. **Remaining arc stops** (tracked, same audit): F1 implementation state machine has no entry, F4 nightly profile forbids PR actions, F5 merge readiness ledger has no writer, F8 no autonomous promoter, F9 convergence state keyed to a non-repeating cycle id, F10 poison-request head-of-line, F11 roles with no minter, F12 human-required context gap, F13/F14 unwired guards.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-690 — the auto-merge gate read a ledger nothing wrote, and the dashboard called every passing run a failure — RESOLVED (this PR, E21-a)

Severity: HIGH (E21-a, the Experiment Bench core). One declared surface, `validation/validation-runs.jsonl`, had TWO writers with different schemas: `validation._run_one` (status/duration_ms/argv) and `validation_runs_ledger.record_validation_run` ($schema/change_id/log_hash/commit_sha/runner_identity, and no `status` at all). Three consequences, each established by EXPERIMENT rather than by reading:

**(1) The dashboard lied, and it was reproduced.** A temp tools dir, the real `record_validation_run` called with `exit_code=0` — a PASSING run — and the real `generate_observability_dashboard` returned `{'run_count': 1, 'failed_count': 1, 'total_duration_ms': 0}`, because `observability.py` counted `status not in ("ok",)` on rows that carry no `status`. **(2) Lane A was dead**: `run_validation_commands`' only caller, `apply_executor_packet`, has zero callers repo-wide (per-name control: `defined=1, refs=0`, measured against a control name returning `refs=3`). **(3) The one that mattered**: `record_validation_run` had NO production writer, while `auto_merge._evaluate_triple_gate` Gate 3 and `validation_matrix_gate` READ it — the merge gate's third assertion was structurally unsatisfiable, the same class as the readiness chain (ORPHAN-680).

A fourth claim was investigated and **withdrawn**: the lead first believed the whole triple gate had no producer, having swept invented names (`record_change_planned/committed/validated`) that do not exist in the repo — a nonexistent name returns zero hits that look exactly like unreachability. The real writers `emit_change_*` are reachable via CLI; Gates 1 and 2 were fine, only Gate 3 lacked a producer. Recorded because a corrected hypothesis is evidence too.

**Fix (agent-implemented on a parallel lane, lead-verified firsthand):** one row schema (`aria/validation-run/v2`) whose required core is derived from what the READERS need, one writer, and `run_experiment` as the first real producer — which makes the triple gate satisfiable. `status` is DERIVED by the writer (`derive_validation_run_status`), never passed; `timeout` is its own status because a killed process produced no exit code, and `exit_code` is `int | None` with `None` required exactly when `timed_out` (enforced both directions). Readers REFUSE (`validation_run_status_missing`) rather than guess — deliberately no derive-from-exit_code fallback, which with a single writer would be dead code that silently rehabilitates a malformed row. Provenance is RESOLVED, not merely non-empty: the change is looked up in the change ledger and the commit through `git rev-parse --verify`, so fabricated provenance cannot reach the ledger. İ1: the duplicate writer is DELETED, not parked beside — `validation.append_jsonl` now raises `validation_surface_owned_elsewhere` on the runs path. The hash-bound logs gained their own declared surface, without which they die at job teardown and the gate then blocks on a run it can no longer verify.

The domain-agnostic contract lands with it: `experiment.py` defines `Experiment{hypothesis, recipe_ref, observation_contract}`, pinned by an AST check that no domain token appears in its identifiers or non-docstring literals — the kernel must not know aquaculture, because the same bench is meant to run against Rust and later an OS. **`docker` remains structurally denied on every path** (`implementation_safety.py` diff empty, `validation.ALLOWED_COMMANDS` byte-identical, and a test registers a `docker compose` recipe and proves it refuses with zero runs recorded): production runs on this host.

**Owner:** claude (session lead) + parallel implementation agent (opus). **Status:** RESOLVED. Named residues, not swept: the lane allowlist has no `cargo`, so a Rust recipe cannot execute yet (own train, explicit decision required); `verify_validation_run` re-hashes the log, so a run older than artifact retention fails verification and blocks the gate (inherited from the original `log_path` design, now applying to every run); `run_experiment` has no cycle-phase or CLI caller yet (E21-b/c); `cli.py --validation-run-ref-json` still lets an operator hand-author refs — the anti-pattern ORPHAN-675 removed elsewhere — left for its own train; `apply_executor_packet` remains callerless.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-688 — ARIA could not find its own most common defect class — RESOLVED (this PR, E9)

Severity: HIGH (E9; the meta-defense tooth). Every one of E8's sixteen findings belonged to four shapes — writer-with-no-reader, reader-with-no-writer, unsatisfiable predicate, unread tunable. A human found all sixteen by reading. No kernel mechanism looked for the SHAPE, so the seventeenth would have cost another human sweep. A system that claims to improve itself cannot outsource its own commonest bug class to its operator.

**Fix (agent-implemented on a parallel lane, lead-verified firsthand) — three teeth.** (1) `surface_reachability` walks argument provenance through the AST and proves which members of a closed vocabulary a production path can WRITE; unreachable members need a manifest waiver carrying owner + reason + expiry + finding, and the suite compares that expiry TO THE CLOCK — the lesson `invariant-reachability.spec.ts` learned expensively when twenty-five waivers sailed a month past a shared deadline in silence. Keyed by surface THEN member, because `ACTIVE` is both a genesis state and a tool status and a flat manifest would let a waiver for one silence a real gap in the other. (2) `kernel-dead-wire-adapter` covers the two masks provenance cannot decide (policy files and argparse are not closed vocabularies with one named writer). (3) `decision_questioning` samples decisions the pipeline already CLOSED and mints one adversarial `verification` envelope each — convergence only ever proved two planners agreed AT DECISION TIME; nothing asked whether the decision still holds against the tree as it stands now.

**Lead-added third-tooth wiring (the residue the agent flagged honestly):** the minter had no cycle phase. Shipping it that way would have reproduced the mechanism-with-no-caller defect INSIDE the fix that hunts it — its own invariant's first catch. It is now a `post_tool` phase, standard-lane only (minting is an action; the burn-in lane's whole claim is that it took none) and `record_and_continue` (self-questioning that crashed asked nothing, which must not cost a night whose real work succeeded), pinned by a roster deliberate-break plus an end-to-end run of the real runner.

**Owner:** claude (session lead) + parallel implementation agents (fable→opus on quota). **Status:** RESOLVED. Carried out, not folded in: the adapter-directory lint debt (ORPHAN-689) is its own train.

**One flagged finding examined and REJECTED, on evidence:** the implementing agent reported the `DISPATCHABLE_ROLES` literal at `tools/aria-poc/ci_executor.py:89` as an İ1 duplication. It is not. The fallback exists for the one mode where the kernel import FAILS — it cannot import the SSoT by definition — and E14 landed a no-drift test that compares the literal to the kernel set, so a narrower copy fails the suite instead of silently making envelopes unclaimable. That is a mirror with a gate (tier 3), not latent duplication, and the gate proved itself here: adding `verification` turned both it and the v7 closed-enum invariant red until the mirror and the enum's expected literal were updated in this same commit, exactly as their comments demand. Recording the rejection rather than quietly dropping it: a finding that was investigated and found wrong is evidence too.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-699 — adjudication panels were mint-once: a dead panel folded to still_escalated forever, and an SLA breach was one report line for eternity — RESOLVED (this PR, X4)

Severity: HIGH (measured on the first real nightly: 9 HUMAN_REQUIRED items breaching SLA since 12-13 Aug, 7 of them lease_lifecycle-shaped and adjudicable). Two dead ends: **(1)** `open_adjudication` was reachable exactly once per escalation — once its 3 envelopes hit the 3-day anchor expiry unclaimed (the executor was disabled, ORPHAN-698), the sweep could only ever fold `still_escalated`, forever; **(2)** the SLA deadline was stamped once and its only reader was a single daily-report line — a breach aged without consequence.

**Fix (X4):** bounded re-open in the sweep's fold branch — when the fold reason is `panel_incomplete:` AND every envelope of the LATEST panel is terminally dead (`derive_request_state` ∈ {ANCHOR_STALE, STALE, EXPIRED}; one live envelope blocks re-open, protecting delivered judge work), a NEW panel row is minted citing its dead predecessor (`reopen_of` + `attempt`), at most MAX_PANEL_REOPENS=2 re-opens (mirroring the claim-requeue budget); exhaustion emits `human_required_adjudication_reopen_exhausted` governance and the sweep payload discloses it — the honest "a human genuinely must act" terminal. The existing one-panel-ever pin passes UNTOUCHED (live panels stay mint-once). SLA breaches now age through the critical_observation N+k·window ladder (derived at render, never stored — append-only preserved): ≥2 windows `escalated`, ≥3 `sustained_breach`, ≥5 `critical_attention`, each amplified in the daily report's HUMAN_REQUIRED section.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-704 — the judgment group key folded the nightly run_id in, so every night re-minted every queued finding: 462 minted, 42 accepted, 296 anchor-dead — RESOLVED (this PR, Y2)

Severity: HIGH (second sealed night, 2026-08-17, measured). `judge_fanout._group_id` was `judge:{tool}:{run}:{finding}` — a fresh `run_id` per nightly adapter run meant the (group, agent) dedupe NEVER matched across nights, so the same finding was re-enveloped every cycle while the executor drained ~9/night; the queue's steady state was a corpse pile (296 ANCHOR_STALE) and `judged_judges` starved behind it. No ceiling existed between the sampler and the queue, and the per-tool `sample_size=5` was hardcoded in the phase.

**Fix (Y2):** the group key is finding-keyed and run-free (`judge:{tool}:{finding_fingerprint}`), making the existing request-ledger dedupe cross-night by construction — the old run-folded behavior is pinned OUT (a re-sampled finding from a new run mints nothing). A second guard skips findings a judge already answered (`already_judged`, from the feedback ledger; re-examining closed verdicts stays the E9 decision-questioning lane's deliberate act). The nightly mint now runs under a per-role pending ceiling with an explicit `mint_skipped_backlog` disclosure surfaced in the phase payload, and both knobs (`sample_size_per_tool`, `max_pending_per_role`) join the genesis policy contract as the `judgment_pipeline` block (POLICY_KEYS + typed accessor + default JSON — an override is mergeable, not dead configuration).

## ORPHAN-HIGH-705 — the drain's four-role priority prefix was itself a starvation topology: every role it omitted queued behind judge volume, structurally unreachable — RESOLVED (this PR, Y4)

Severity: HIGH (second sealed night, 2026-08-17, measured). `ci_executor_drain._PRIORITY_ROLES` named four planning roles; everything else — `maintenance_utility` (the autonomy planner), `consensus_arbitration`, `human_required_adjudication`, `verification`, the rest — rode the role=None fallback, oldest-first, behind 64 judge envelopes at ~7-9 drains/night. The X1 pin even asserted this shape as correct ("judge + adjudication roles are NOT in priority — they ride the fallback"), which was true and insufficient: the fallback was a queue those roles could never reach the head of.

**Fix (Y4):** `_ROLE_QUOTA_ORDER` names EVERY drained role in arc order (planning lane first, judges last), and the drain runs a QUOTA ROUND first — each waiting role gets exactly one guaranteed slot per run — before the fallback spends the remaining budget in the same arc order with role=None as the final catch-all. The X1 topology pin is DELIBERATELY rewritten (İ2): coverage is now asserted role-by-role against `DISPATCHABLE_ROLES` (drafter roles excepted — the skill-genesis lane consumes those), `maintenance_utility` rides the arc by name, and resurrecting the old narrow prefix breaks the pin. The next-pending selection is extracted into `_next_pending_for_role` so the quota round and fallback share one query path.

The bridge-status ledger gains its first reader: reflection's new **Bridge Health** section renders the role×transition matrix and top error signatures whenever any transition is non-ok — twelve silent fold failures can never be invisible again.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-707 — the declared output-artifact surface matched nothing the writer writes, and result rows pointed at absolute host paths: every cross-run bridge replay died envelope-unreadable — RESOLVED (this PR, Y6)

## ORPHAN-HIGH-712 — ARIA's memory shared a workspace with an hourly `git clean -ffdx`, and a deleted store bypassed every unpublished-work protection silently — RESOLVED (this PR, Z1)

(c) `checkout_state_store` detects the registered-but-missing worktree and discloses `state_store_rematerialized_after_missing` on the freshly restored store — the disclosure itself rides the next publish; a vanished store can never again be silent.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-703 — the dispatch hook abandoned every failed claim to lease expiry, and both planner idempotency filters counted the corpses as live — RESOLVED (this PR, Y1+Y3)

Severity: HIGH (second sealed night, 2026-08-17, measured: 106 `lease_expired` requeues; every planner HUMAN_REQUIRED escalation carried the identical `claimed→stale→requeued`×3 signature; `convergence: None`, zero implementations). Two coupled defects. **(Y1)** `planner_dispatch_hook.py` claimed, spawned `ci_executor.py` with `timeout_seconds = lease_seconds + 60` — the lease was ALREADY DEAD before the subprocess timeout could fire — and released on NO failure path: TimeoutExpired and non-zero exit both returned with the claim held, so the next cycle's reaper charged `lease_expired` to the REQUEST's budget, three strikes, HUMAN_REQUIRED. **(Y3)** `plan_round_controller._ensure_planner_request` and `autonomy_orchestrator._find_projected_queue_request` matched ANY prior request regardless of derived state, so a round whose envelope died of queue mechanics was wedged forever — nothing ever re-minted, the plan could never converge.

**Fix (Y1):** the child's wall-clock budget sits strictly inside the lease (`_executor_timeout_seconds = max(300, lease−120)`), and every failure exit releases through `_release_abandoned_claim` — pre-checked against the claims ledger so a child that already released is a recorded skip, not a duplicate released+requeued pair. Both new release reasons (`planner_dispatch_executor_timeout`, `planner_dispatch_executor_exit_nonzero`) are HARNESS-class: a killed child says nothing about the request, so its requeue budget is never burned. **Fix (Y3):** the closed set `REMINT_ELIGIBLE_DEAD_STATES` ({HUMAN_REQUIRED, ANCHOR_STALE, STALE, CANCELLED, EXPIRED} — ACCEPTED/REJECTED stay out, they are verdicts about the work) makes both filters state-aware: live-or-outcome matches short-circuit as before; an all-dead match mints a successor with `remint_of` lineage (the field participates in the request-id fold, so a successor gets a fresh id while a repeat re-mint of the same corpse stays idempotent), budgeted at 2 mirroring `DEFAULT_MAX_REQUEUES`, then an honest `planner_request_remint_exhausted` / `next_cycle_queue_item_remint_exhausted` disclosure.

Configuration is the `watchdog_pull` policy block; the base URL is machine-local and lives in the operator override, and the API key NEVER enters policy or ledgers — only the NAME of the env var the runner exports. E24-b (on-host docker-log collector) stays gated on the first pull-detector finding surviving triage, per plan.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-693 — a reproduced defect could not change what ARIA believed about it: the finding fold spoke one event type — RESOLVED (this PR, E21-c)

Severity: HIGH (E21-c, the Deney Masası's promotion arc). The finding ledger was event-sourced in name only: `_replay_findings` skipped every row whose `event` was not `finding_emitted`, so a finding was frozen at mint forever. Three consequences, each measured on 2026-08-16: **(1)** certainty was a caste system — `CONFIRMED` sat at the top of the vocabulary with ZERO producers (and `SUSPECTED`/`UNCERTAIN`/`UNKNOWN` beside it, equally producerless: three of five members were words nothing could utter); **(2)** STATUSES had readers (`cycle_guard` counts OPEN|IN_PROGRESS, `debt.py:242` expects RESOLVED, `handoff_ledger` closes on WITHDRAWN) but replay could never reach any state but OPEN — a state machine whose states were unreachable; **(3)** an experiment that re-ran a defect red (E21-a/b) changed NOTHING: the observation row existed, the finding stayed OBSERVED, and the next night's judges re-derived from scratch what the bench had already proven.

**Fix (E21-c):** the fold speaks a CLOSED four-member vocabulary and REFUSES unknown types (silent skip is data loss in a compatibility costume). `finding_reproduced` — matched RED run (`timeout` refused, it is environment noise) of an experiment that DECLARED `finding_ref` at registration (no post-hoc stapling) — is the first producer of `certainty=CONFIRMED`: certainty is earned by reproduction, not asserted. `finding_fix_verified` — the SAME recipe re-runs matched GREEN with resolved provenance — lands directly on RESOLVED with `closes_in_commit` from the run row; a red rerun after resolution is refused as a REGRESSION deserving its own finding. Operator transitions ride `finding_status_changed` through the closed `STATUS_TRANSITIONS` map (RESOLVED/WITHDRAWN terminal, banned-phrase gate on reasons). İ2: `SUSPECTED`/`UNCERTAIN`/`UNKNOWN` are REMOVED, pinned by a deliberate-breakage test — a future grade re-enters only in the PR that adds its producer. The memory leg closes the loop through the single belief writer (İ1): a matched red run on a bound experiment becomes a `finding-reproduced-f-xxx` belief citing the finding's own scope files, so reproduction outlives the night. Fix-verified bindings are permanent (`list_fix_verified_bindings`) — the green recipe is the regression fixture, re-run through the SAME experiment lane (no third fixture system); the E21-d night phase is its consumer. CLI: `experiment register|run|reproduce|verify-fix|finding-status|regression-bindings` — `experiment run` is `run_experiment`'s first production caller, closing E21-a residue 3.

**E21-d (same train) — the night runs the bench.** `experiment_night.py`: two budgeted lanes (3 problem + 3 regression per night, skips DISCLOSED in the payload). The problem lane selects only contracts that can ONLY match on a red run (`status_equals failed` / non-zero `exit_code_equals`) so a finding's SOLUTION experiment is never misread as an unproven hypothesis; it opens the finding's change-chain (`emit_change_planned`, idempotent — problem run, fix commit and green re-run join on ONE spine) and promotes matched red runs through the E21-c bridge. The regression lane re-runs fix-verified recipes; a red rerun emits `experiment_regression_detected` governance (judgment lanes own the response — no reflex finding mint). Registered as CyclePhase `experiment_night` with the EXISTING `WRITES_PERMITTED` precondition and `record_and_continue`. The integration test (real runner, real subprocess) caught a latent crash class merged audits missed: under `ARIA_REPO_STATE_ROOT` every `emit_finding`/`emit_debt` died on `relative_to(repo)` because the durable store lives outside the repo tree — four sites fixed (`finding.py` governance path + `_refresh_index`, and their `debt.py` twins), paths now resolve against the store that owns them.

**Owner:** claude (session lead). **Deadline:** landed. **Status:** RESOLVED (this PR).

## ORPHAN-MEDIUM-689 — seven ARIA adapters carry 55 ESLint errors because no lint target reaches their directory — OPEN

Severity: MEDIUM. `tools/aria-adapters/**` is not an Nx project, and `npm run lint` is `nx affected --target=lint` — so every adapter written there has been unlinted since the directory was created. Measured on 2026-08-15: **55 errors across all seven adapters plus their test files** — `import/order` group separation, a `no-console` in each test harness, a `no-base-to-string` and an unused binding in the TypeORM adapter, and one shared idiom repeated seven times (`readStdin` concatenating `string | Buffer` after `setEncoding('utf8')`, which `restrict-plus-operands` rejects). None of it is new debt from any single change; it is the accumulated cost of a directory outside the gate.

**Root cause is the GATE GAP, not the errors** — fixing 55 errors by hand leaves the directory unlinted and the fifty-sixth arrives with the next adapter. The architectural fix is to bring `tools/aria-adapters` under a lint target (its own Nx project or an explicit path in the repo-wide lint script), then clear the debt the gate reports. The E9 adapter (`kernel-dead-wire-adapter.ts`) landed clean and narrows the chunk type at the boundary, which is the shape its six siblings should converge on.

**Owner:** claude (session lead). **Deadline:** 2026-09-15. **Status:** RESOLVED (this PR) — the GATE first: `tools/aria-adapters/project.json` registers an Nx `lint` target (heap-bumped eslint, `--max-warnings=0`), so `nx affected --target=lint` reaches the directory and the fifty-sixth error cannot arrive unlinted. Then the debt the gate reported: 32 import/order autofixed; the seven-sibling `readStdin` idiom converged on the E9 adapter's boundary-narrowing shape; 8 `no-console` in self-test harnesses became `process.stdout.write`; 4 indent-argument `JSON.stringify` sites dropped the indent; the truly dead `secondArg` binding was DELETED (İ2 — not underscore-parked); one `String()`-on-object coercion became a type narrow; one missing return type annotated. All nine adapter self-tests pass unchanged.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-775 — branch-protection proofs had no producer and no row to cite: the probe's evidence died with the process — RESOLVED (this PR, F5-b)

> Renumbered 2026-08-20 from a triple-booked `ORPHAN-HIGH-694` (the Alertmanager routing entry kept
> the number; the `readiness_proofs.py:1004` F5-g comment and this entry both claimed it too — the
> PROC-HIGH-015 collision class, instance recorded under PROC-HIGH-015 on 2026-08-20).

Severity: HIGH (readiness-claim chain, family 2 of 8). `record_branch_protection_proof` had zero production callers (only F5-a's workflow-run family produced anything), and there existed NO ledger row a branch-protection proof's `source_ledger_ref` could resolve into — `preflight.verify_branch_protection` probed gh-api and threw the payload away, so the strongest evidence about merge safety evaporated with the process. The claim verifier demands a v3 proof (snapshot_hash, measured booleans, ruleset_ids, empty bypass_actors, resolvable source ref) — structurally unsatisfiable.

**Fix (F5-b):** ONE probe (İ1) — `preflight.probe_branch_protection` returns verdict + reasons + RAW payload; `verify_branch_protection` becomes its thin projection (pinned by a source-inspection test: no second `subprocess.run`). New declared surface `enterprise/branch-protection-snapshots.jsonl` (observation-class) persists the payload with canonical sha256; `readiness_proofs.produce_branch_protection_proof` mints the proof whose EVERY field is measured from that snapshot — `required_checks` from `required_status_checks.contexts`, signature/review/conversation/force-push/delete booleans from their payload blocks, `ruleset_ids` + `bypass_actors` from the gh-api rules probe (probe failure raises: silence must never read as "no bypass actors"). A weakly-protected repo yields `valid=false` recorded HONESTLY — measurement here, policy at the claim gate. CLI: `readiness produce-branch-protection-proof`. 6 new tests incl. the honest-weakness path and source-ref resolution via `find_row_by_source_ledger_ref`.

**F5-c..g (same train — the chain closes).** Family by family, each with its own commit: **F5-d** — `acquire_remote_cas_lease` (full CAS semantics, epoch fencing) had ZERO callers; the proof producer is its first, and a foreign fresh lease fails closed. **F5-e** — a REAL `git bundle` of the target ref, verified by `git bundle verify` (the simulation IS git), archived byte-identically under the retention store; both proofs carry measured, "sha256:"-prefixed digest pairs and tools-root-relative uris the verifier re-reads. **F5-c** — the token proof measures workflow_hash from the YAML bytes, contract_hash from the registry SSoT, write-paths/network-policy from the pinned job contract, and the lease MODE from the mint itself; a PAT-fallback lease records valid=false with every fallback flag true — the claim then fails until the GH App secrets exist, which is the truth. **F5-f** — the plan had parked DLP behind an operator waiver, but the evaluator cannot be waived, so the ROOT fix landed instead: a closed, deterministic secret-pattern scanner (private-key blocks, provider token prefixes, credential assignments) over the five required surfaces; findings carry pattern NAME and location, never the matched bytes; a vacuous scan (missing surface) fails closed. **F5-g** — `record_enterprise_readiness_claim`'s first production caller: deterministic claim-id allocation, all seven families threaded, the waiver sweep attested through `ci_source`'s first production writer, and ONLY ledger-proven workflow-run ids admitted. The integration test assembles a full claim from produced evidence and passes `verify_enterprise_readiness` with a live adapter — **auto-merge's third condition is structurally satisfiable in production for the first time.**

**Owner:** claude (session lead). **Deadline:** landed. **Status:** RESOLVED (this PR).

## ORPHAN-HIGH-687 — every judge re-read the same evidence files the envelope could have quoted — RESOLVED (this PR, E17-b)

Severity: HIGH (E17-b, the mint-side half of context economy). The envelope carried repository_map, established_knowledge and recent_intent — but ZERO file content, so every judge opened each `evidence_refs` file itself, and the adversarial judge re-read the same files a second time by design. The counter-pattern already existed in-repo (cross-reviewer embeds plan text inline with a content hash, "no file Read required"); evidence never got it.

**Fix (agent-implemented on a parallel lane, lead-verified firsthand):** new `evidence_excerpts.excerpts_for_refs` packs bounded excerpts (±40 lines, 8KB/ref, 64KB total) reusing the existing ref parser and canonical-path resolver (İ1 — no second copy); 7 STRUCTURAL skip reasons (cap exhausted, unreadable, …) so a dropped excerpt is always named, never silent. The mint attaches `evidence_excerpts` beside its sibling sections, the renderer emits `<untrusted_evidence_excerpt path lines content_hash>` with the verification law — verify against the excerpt, Read the file ONLY on hash mismatch or insufficiency, and say which — with the tag body byte-identical to the hashed bytes. `PROMPT_RENDER_VERSION` 2→3 with the section gated on v3 (no-legacy-mint discipline), the field added to the fused-envelope key set and the planner serialiser, and the budget gate gained a distinct excerpt component.

**Scope note carried honestly:** no production caller passed `context_repo_root`, so the feature would have been DORMANT on the judge lane it exists for; the fix threads `repo_root` from the judgment-pipeline phase — which as a side effect also activates the FAZ-4 `recent_intent` section on that lane, dormant since it landed. Stated here rather than discovered later. 30 tests incl. the drop-from-fused-projection, oversized-set and post-mint-tamper deliberate breaks; full kernel suite 3924 passed + 573 subtests.

**Owner:** claude (session lead) + parallel implementation agent. **Status:** RESOLVED. NOT done (named, not skipped): the four judge `.md` prompts still describe reading files directly — telling judges they may rely on the excerpt touches model-tier-protected files and is its own change.

## ORPHAN-MEDIUM-692 — the bench could only run the two languages the lane knew, and its evidence could be an amputated log or a cache hit — RESOLVED (this PR, E21-b)

Severity: MEDIUM (E21-b). E21-a landed a domain-agnostic experiment contract whose kernel is pinned domain-blind by an AST check. But the execution lane's allowlist knew only `npm`, `npx` and `python3`, so **a Rust recipe could not run at all** — the domain-agnostic claim rested on the kernel not naming a domain, never on a second language actually executing. An assertion, not a result.

**Fix (agent-implemented on a parallel lane, lead-verified firsthand): the Rust lane opens narrowly.** `cargo` joins `validation.ALLOWED_COMMANDS` restricted to the non-mutating verbs `check` and `test`; `publish`, `install`, `run` and every other subcommand are refused, as is `--config`, which can turn an approved verb into arbitrary argv via a runner override. Precedent, not new privilege: `implementation_safety.ALLOWED_BASH_COMMANDS` already carried `cargo test` for the fixture runner, and this lane is strictly tighter than that one. `docker` remains structurally denied (`implementation_safety.py` diff is empty and the refusal test still passes). Lead probed all seven cases independently — the two allowed forms accepted, `publish`/`install`/`run`/`--config`/`docker compose` each refused with a named reason.

**Recipes are DATA.** A manifest under `tools/aria-poc/` (the repo-facing lane that already knows this repository) plus a thin registrar; adding a recipe is a data edit, never a kernel change. A gate spec proves every manifest command is executable by the lane, using the lane's own parser rather than a second copy of the allowlist.

**Two defects the RUNNING found, which reading would not have.** (1) The first TypeScript run recorded `exit_code=0` while its hash-bound log held 63 KB of a 161 KB run, cut mid-escape-sequence — 80 of 124 suites and the whole summary missing, because nx's default TUI writer emits redraw frames rather than a stream. The kernel does not truncate (`_write_run_log` writes the full captured stdout/stderr; the capture has no cap), so the honest fix is at the recipe layer: `--output-style=stream`. (2) The second run returned `exit_code=0` in seconds from `[local cache]` **having executed nothing** — a bench that can be answered by a build cache records greens it never earned. Both are now pinned by the manifest gate, including `test_no_recipe_can_be_answered_from_a_build_cache`.

**Both recipes ran end to end, green, with real ledger rows.** Rust: `cargo check -p alarm-core`, `exit_code=0`, `status=ok`, `duration_ms=1307`, observation `matched=true`, and `verify_validation_run` re-hashed the log successfully. TypeScript: `npx nx run-many --target=test --projects=backend-common --skip-nx-cache --output-style=stream` → 124 suites, 1369 tests, including ORPHAN-691's own regression specs — so the first solution-experiment the bench ever ran verifies the previous finding's fix.

**Schedulability, measured twice (agent and lead independently):** the Rust recipe costs **~96 KB of disk and 1.39 s**, producing a 156 KB `target/` — it compiles one dependency-free crate to rmeta. Safe for a nightly trigger. The TypeScript recipe costs ~40 MB of `.nx` growth per run — also acceptable, but not free. This measurement is mandatory after the 2026-08-15 incident, where the host filled and the kernel's own disk floor blocked every push.

**Owner:** claude (session lead) + parallel implementation agent (opus). **Status:** RESOLVED. Named residues: the crate is `alarm-core`, the shared alarm decision core, NOT the `suderra-agent` edge binary — checking the binary would compile tokio/reqwest/rustls/rumqttc, gigabytes, so the Rust lane is proven on the workspace's small member and the binary remains unmeasured; `npx nx test <project>` is refused by the lane (only `affected`/`run-many` forms are admitted), so recipes use `run-many`; cold-runner cost of the cargo recipe (fresh registry index) was not measured, only the warm path.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-691 — the tenant-isolation watchdog reported ten schemas clean that it was never allowed to read — RESOLVED (this PR)

Severity: HIGH (security-relevant: the mechanism is the platform's standing check for tenant data contamination). Found while tracing why the production disk hit 99%.

**How it surfaced.** `aqua-auth`'s container log had grown to 960 MB and the host was down to 2.1 GB free. Sampling the logs (not guessing) showed two unrelated producers. The second one mattered more: `aqua-postgres` was emitting a continuous stream of `ERROR: permission denied for schema ...` — 1616 occurrences in the last 4000 lines, spread over sensor (469), admin (424), hr (208), alert, messaging, auth, billing, event_store, ai and notification. The statements were `SELECT COUNT(*) as cnt FROM "admin"."tenant_activities"` and siblings, which match `SourceSchemaScanner` exactly, and that scanner is wired in one place only: `farm-service`, on a ten-minute cron.

**The defect.** `farm-service` connects as the `farm_service` role, which by design has no grants on other services' schemas — but the scanner iterates ALL of `MODULE_SCHEMAS`. Every denied query landed in a catch-all whose comment reads _"Table might not exist in source schema yet (service not started)"_ and whose body is a `logger.debug`. Permission denial and not-yet-created were therefore indistinguishable, so the scan returned zero violations for ten schemas it never read, and the runner recorded a completed, clean attestation. A safety mechanism that reports success for what it could not see is worse than one switched off, because the report is believed. The coverage counter compounded it: `schemasScanned` added `MODULE_SCHEMAS.length` unconditionally, so the report also claimed eleven source schemas scanned when one was readable.

Notably the sibling `CrossTenantProbe` already fails CLOSED — it throws on an unreadable table. The correct idiom lived in the same directory; the scanner was the outlier.

**Fix.** A new `UNVERIFIABLE_SCHEMA` violation type (HIGH): a schema the scan could not read is reported as a gap in coverage, never as clean. SQLSTATE is now decisive — `42P01` (undefined_table) stays benign, which is what the original catch was written for; `42501` (insufficient_privilege), `3F000` and any unknown driver error become findings that name what could not be checked and why. A one-round-trip `has_schema_privilege` pre-check per schema replaces the N doomed `COUNT(*)`s, which is what kept postgres logging ~1600 error lines per cycle. `schemasScanned` counts only schemas actually read. The scanner now depends on the narrow `SchemaQueryExecutor` shape it actually uses, so the regression suite drives real refusals through a plain object with no cast.

**Verification (experiment, not reading):** 6 tests, and the deliberate-break was RUN — restoring the old catch-all and removing the pre-check turns 4 of the 6 red, while the two asserting already-correct behaviour (benign missing table, real contamination still reported) stay green. That signature is the proof the suite measures the defect rather than the implementation.

**Second producer, same incident, separate root cause:** `DATABASE_LOGGING=true` was set on a production service with `NODE_ENV=production`, so TypeORM echoed every statement; measured at 1.9 lines/second ≈ 164k lines/day from auth-service alone. Nothing was writing data — the volume was statement echo from the outbox poller. `resolveDatabaseLogging` now withholds per-statement logging in production (errors, warnings, migrations and schema events still log) unless `DATABASE_QUERY_LOGGING_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true` says so by name. 5 tests, including that the acknowledgement is not itself a second switch.

**Owner:** claude (session lead). **Status:** RESOLVED in code. Two operational residues, named because they are NOT closed by this PR: (1) the fix reaches production only when the containers are recreated, and `docker compose` currently cannot recreate anything — `docker-compose.droplet.yml` has required `SENTINEL_HUB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` since `a297b45dd` (2026-08-01) and neither `.env` nor the running containers carry it, so interpolation fails for every service; the live containers date from 2026-07-14. (2) Those containers were also created with no `LogConfig` limits at all, so rotation defined in compose (`max-size: 20m`, present on all 37 real services) has never applied to them, and there is no `/etc/docker/daemon.json` default either. Both need an operator decision.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-685 — every judge spawn cold-read 125KB of contract docs to do a 3KB job — RESOLVED (this PR, E17-a)

Severity: HIGH (E17-a). The four runtime-dispatched agents (evidence-judge, adversarial-judge, cross-reviewer, worker) each opened their turn by reading SPEC.md (43,191 B) + CONTRACTS.md (70,488 B) + PIPELINES.md (5,937 B) + layer-1-aria.md (6,119 B) = **125,735 bytes** — before seeing a single finding. With judge fan-out ≥2 per sampled finding, a night paid that toll dozens of times for laws that fit in a few KB.

**Fix (agent-implemented on a parallel lane, lead-verified firsthand):** a GENERATED digest, never a hand-maintained copy — `<!-- judge-digest:begin/end -->` markers mark the passages a runtime judge actually needs inside the SSoT docs, `contract_digest.render_judge_digest` extracts and composes `docs/aria/generated/JUDGE-DIGEST.md` with a `source_hash` over the concatenated marked sources plus anchor pointers ("if the digest is insufficient, Read the anchor you followed — and cite it"). A >10KB render RAISES: the digest cannot silently bloat back into the thing it replaced. Final size **8,723 B** (headroom 1,517). The four preambles now reference the digest + the layer-2 envelope; planner/drafter agents are untouched (plan-writing lanes keep full SSoT). Invariant test: committed digest ≡ render output byte-for-byte, source_hash recomputes, the four .mds no longer @-ref SPEC/CONTRACTS, and deliberate-breaks for a mutated marked source and a synthetic oversized digest.

The finishing agent also caught and corrected a FALSE EVIDENCE CLAIM in the first draft's comments (they asserted the cost was already measured by the budget audit; it was not — that counting is E17-d's job, which had not landed at the time) and regenerated the stale `format-scope.json` manifest that would have failed CI. Honesty discipline held under handoff.

**Landing addendum (same PR):** the digest's first CI run exposed a THIRD defect, in the docs gate itself — `markdownlint-changed` lints whole files, so adding eight marker comments to SPEC/CONTRACTS/PIPELINES dragged ~300 pre-existing MD013/MD040 violations into scope and failed the PR. Reflowing a 70KB contract doc to satisfy a rule it never met is churn on the very SSoT the doc is. The gate now bills only findings on lines the change actually wrote (`git diff -U0` ranges), reports inherited debt without failing, and excludes `docs/**/generated/**` entirely (a generated artifact reproduces its sources byte-for-byte; it cannot be re-wrapped without breaking the identity an invariant pins). This mirrors the format gate's existing base-debt quarantine — new lines enforced, inherited debt attributed. Pinned by a stub-linter fixture test.

**Owner:** claude (session lead) + parallel implementation agents (fable→opus handoff on quota). **Status:** RESOLVED. Note for readers: these four agents no longer load `layer-1-aria.md` — permitted by the prompt-contract carve-out, a deliberate narrowing for runtime lanes only.

## ORPHAN-MEDIUM-684 — no service could ever get its own auditor: finding density had no consumer — RESOLVED (this PR, E15-c)

Severity: MEDIUM (E15-c; the BP2 precursor). E15-a/b gave findings a service dimension and the reports a per-service view, but nothing ACTED on it: a service drowning in open findings could never acquire a specialist of its own, because the genesis request lane (`learning._emit_genesis_for_gap`) mints only from capability gaps — service finding-density was a number nobody consumed.

The finishing agent found and closed a real defect in the first draft: the producer ignored `max_requests_per_cycle`, so the operator's configured genesis ceiling would have become untrue the first night several services crossed at once — it now ranks sickest-first, caps, reports `eligible_count`/`capped_count`, and suppressed services never spend cap budget (deliberate-break test: cap=1 with two qualifying services keeps only the sickest). 14 tests.

Noted, NOT silently fixed: `reflection.py`/`finding.py`/`task.py` repeat the "stored services else derive" idiom on the finding DOC shape — pre-existing E15-a debt, tracked for the E15 follow-up.

(2) New `usage_ledger.record_context_usage` + declared surface `knowledge-graph/context-usage.jsonl` (kg-block late-joiner style; the roster sweep sees the deliberate literal and resolves it — no exclusion): rows carry input/output + `cache_creation`/`cache_read` tokens per (request, role, target*agent, model); a None-usage call records NOTHING via an explicit structural-skip branch. ## ORPHAN-HIGH-686 — ten dead role contracts, three agents nobody could dispatch, and a whole module nothing called — RESOLVED (this PR, E14)

Severity: HIGH (E14 role hygiene). `agent_surface.REQUEST_ROLES` declared 22 roles; ten had no production minter — dead contracts that make the surface a wish list instead of a map. Worse, three of them had READY AGENTS waiting (goldset-curator, change-intelligence, consensus-arbiter) that no code path could ever invoke.

**Fix (agent-implemented on a parallel lane, lead-verified firsthand) — three real minters:** `goldset_curation` fires when a tool's proposal reaches `ready` (a blocked proposal mints nothing — the curator could only repeat the blocker at LLM cost); `change_intelligence` mints per merged PR, newest-first under a budget so the first activation cannot bill the historical backlog in one night; `consensus_arbitration` mints on a judge split. **Five removed with evidence:** implementation_review, architectural_arbitration, auth_security_review, access_boundary_review, tenant_isolation_review had zero producers AND zero consumers repo-wide — provenance traced to a 2026-05 plan whose lanes shipped differently (the auth lane became the security-boundary adapter + spine gate; domain review became `specialist_domain_review`). Removed from REQUEST_ROLES, ROLE_TARGET_PAIRING and the cap table (replaced by the cap of the role actually minted), with the whitelist trimmed only where the dead role was an agent's ONLY kernel dispatch path.

**Three defects the work uncovered and closed:** (1) all three revived roles were missing from `DISPATCHABLE_ROLES` — minting alone would have produced envelopes no executor may claim (plus pre-existing drift: `human_required_adjudication` was missing from the executor's fallback literal too); (2) the entire `pr_tracking` module was unreachable — no production caller anywhere — so the merge trigger had to be built on the live `pr-lifecycle` ledger, and `plan_pr_impact` now executes on real ledgers for the first time; (3) a DUPLICATE arbitration path: judge disagreement already escalated to HUMAN_REQUIRED whose panel dispatches the same arbiter — İ1 applied, the escalation now defers while an arbiter request is in flight (arbitration first, operator as fallback, nothing dropped, only ordered).

**Owner:** claude (session lead) + parallel implementation agent (opus). **Status:** RESOLVED. Honest flags carried into the PR: the arbiter's vote is a third ai_judge row, so an unweighted 2–1 group stays escalated (fail-closed) until calibration weights exist.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-676 — the genesis lifecycle had no producer AND its human gate demanded evidence nothing could mint — RESOLVED (this PR, C4-c)

Severity: HIGH (C4-c). Two locks on one door. SANDBOX-family states stay deliberately out of this producer's reach — their proof chain is C4-d. 6 tests incl. the first-production-chain and shadow-out-of-reach deliberate-breaks.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED. Next: C4-d real-mode eval bridge (REAL_SANDBOX/SHADOW/EVAL_WINDOW proofs).

## ORPHAN-HIGH-673 — nothing stopped a weaker model from authoring or overwriting a stronger model's agents — RESOLVED (this PR, E16)

Severity: HIGH (operator rule 2026-08-13: "Fable'ın yazdığı agent'ı Opus/Sonnet silemesin; Sonnet falan agent yazamasın"). The genesis materialize path — the one kernel path that writes agent files — carried no notion of WHICH model authored an agent and no floor on which model may author one. When genesis goes live (C4), a low-tier drafter could have overwritten a Fable-authored agent, and knowledge loss would have been one-directional and silent. The model-agnostic principle (models are pluggable, mechanisms are the asset) requires the inverse guarantee: a stronger model's work survives weaker successors AND predecessors.

**Fix:** `MODEL_TIER_ORDER` (fable > opus > sonnet > haiku) + `MIN_AGENT_AUTHORING_TIER = opus` join `agent_runtime_profile` as the single tier SSoT. Unknown models resolve ASYMMETRICALLY by design: as a target's author they rank strongest (a stamp this kernel does not know is most plausibly a FUTURE model — protected), as an active actor they rank weakest (an actor that cannot prove its tier may neither author nor modify). `materialize_agent_draft` now (1) resolves the authoring model from the drafter's frontmatter SSoT (readable, not claimable), (2) refuses below-floor authoring (`agent_authoring_tier_too_low`), (3) refuses overwriting a file whose `authored_by_model` outranks the author (`model_tier_insufficient_to_modify` — the duel has NO exception; that path escalates to HUMAN_REQUIRED), and (4) kernel-injects the `authored_by_model` stamp, overwriting any drafter-supplied value — measured at mint, never claimed. Unstamped legacy agents stay modifiable: the rule protects provenance that exists, it does not invent it. 14 tests incl. the sonnet-cannot-author and weaker-cannot-overwrite deliberate-breaks and the forged-stamp correction.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED. NOT this PR (plan-ordered, C4-a..d refined map in the program plan): the genesis transition producers, operator-provenance writer, fixture_results assembler and the HUMAN_REQUIRED coverage-shape mismatch — each its own train.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-672 — the organism had no environment sense: a full disk read as chain corruption, and the label backlog was invisible — RESOLVED (this PR, E18+E20)

Severity: HIGH (E18 lived 2026-08-13: the host hit 98% disk; ledger writes died with ENOSPC that surfaced as six phantom unittest errors and an integrity-shaped verify failure — hours of misdiagnosis). Two structural gaps. (E18) The kernel had ZERO capacity awareness: no disk precondition in `verify_preflight` (sandbox + node_modules were the only environment members), and the read path reported ANY OSError as ledger invalidity (`verify_jsonl` returned `valid: False` with no fault class; `load_jsonl_verified` raised plain `LedgerIntegrityError`) — an environment fault masqueraded as corruption. (E20) The labeling economy's unlabeled half was invisible: `record_seeding_finding` grew the seeding corpus on every live finding, `list_corpus_status` reported only the LABELED corpus and only via a buried CLI, and the daily report never mentioned the backlog — the calibration bottleneck (how much operator label work waits) had no surface anywhere.

**Fix (E18):** `verify_preflight` gains a measured disk precondition — `_free_disk_gb` (`shutil.disk_usage`) against `MIN_FREE_DISK_GB` (env `ARIA_MIN_FREE_DISK_GB`, default 5); a MEASURED low disk appends `disk_low:free_gb=…` + `environment_preconditions_not_met`, an unprobeable disk deliberately does not block. Zero new plumbing downstream: the reason flows through the existing `preflight_standard_warnings` governance kind straight into the daily anchor's blocked-reason surface (Tier-2). The read path now names the fault: `verify_jsonl` returns `reason_kind: "io_error"` + `errno`, `load_jsonl_verified`'s message carries `reason_kind=io_error` — corruption and environment are distinguishable without parsing errno strings. No YAML df step: the kernel preflight is the single owner (a workflow copy would be İ1 duplication). **(E20):** new `list_seeding_backlog` (read-only resolver — a reader neither creates state nor demands identity) reports per-tool seeded/labeled/unlabeled by fingerprint; the report's label-queue section renders a "Seeding backlog" block — including when the judgment-sample queue is empty (the two halves are independent), while keeping the empty-heading discipline when nothing waits at all.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-667 — two safety constants disagreed and the first live drain lost 30/30 spawns to their argument — RESOLVED (this PR, executor-smoke finding)

Severity: HIGH (found by the first executor smoke, run 31704817330 — the iteration doing its job on a NEW lane). The spawn budget gate (ORPHAN-660) shipped with a hardcoded default estimate of $1.50; the genesis policy's own `per_run` cap is $0.50. Every drained request hit `cost_budget_per_run_cap_exceeded` BEFORE its spawn started: `attempted: 30, failed: 30`, the cost breaker tripped on CONFIGURATION rather than on spend, and 30 requests were left claimed-in-flight. The gate's job is to stop a night that would blow the budget — not to referee a disagreement between two constants.

**Fix:** the default estimate DERIVES from the policy — 80% of the operative `per_run` cap (`_load_caps`, same resolution path the enforcement uses, so the two can never disagree again). The env override (`ARIA_ESTIMATED_RUN_USD`) remains for operators who know a lane's real per-run cost; a malformed override falls back to the derived value. The gate still refuses honestly when projected daily/monthly spend is actually exhausted — which is its purpose. New deliberate-break test: an untouched environment passes the gate (pre-fix it could not); gate + deadline suites green (11). Residue noted: the tripped breaker state persists in the published store and gates only `autonomous`-profile preflight (current lanes run `standard`); `aria-kernel breaker reset` is the operator verb, queued for the pre-cron cleanup.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED.

## ORPHAN-HIGH-666 — the night could never be completed: tenant-scoping's honest flood tripped a silent output cap — RESOLVED (this PR, smoke-run 4 finding)

Severity: HIGH (found by smoke runs 1-4 — the ONE non-green tool in four consecutive live nights). `tenant-scoping-adapter` returned `budget_exceeded` at ~70s every night, which `non_ok_tools` turned into a permanent cycle="failed": no night could ever seal `completed`. The cause was not time: the runner's `output_too_large` branch reuses the `budget_exceeded` status when stdout exceeds `STDOUT_PARSE_MAX_BYTES` (5 MB), and the full-repo tenant scan honestly emits 5.84 MB — 66 findings plus **11,471 observations** (9,363 `tenant_repository_call`). The actionable channel was tiny; the telemetry drowned it, and the drowning wore a misleading label.

**Fix (both sides of the class):** (runner) the cap moves to 12 MB — measured reality × 2, with the measurement in the comment; (adapter) observations get a deterministic per-type cap (3,000, applied post-sort on stable ids) with the drop DECLARED per type in `metadata.observations_truncated` — honest truncation, never silent (live: 2.5 MB, 66 findings unchanged, `tenant_repository_call: 6363 dropped` declared). Findings are never capped. Verified live: full-repo run at 2.5 MB with identical findings; adapter unit tests green; runner suites green.

**Owner:** claude (this session). **Status:** RESOLVED.
